findings.confidence: Verified primary text with scope interpretation

findings.entity: BC and Ontario business companies and federal CBCA
findings.finding: CRA confirms participating business incorporations in BC, Ontario and federally receive a business number and corporation income tax program account automatically. Other program accounts require separate assessment.
findings.section: Incorporate your business; After you register
findings.effective_or_version: Page updated 2026-06-30; program commencement not established
findings.unresolved: Actual account receipt, activity-dependent registrations and tax advice depend on the organization.
findings.product_implication: Capture receipt and identifiers; do not create duplicate BN/RC accounts or mark all tax registrations complete.

findings.finding: CRA provides a separate registered-charity application and review process. Incorporation must be kept separate from charitable registration in the product.
findings.unresolved: Charitable purposes, qualification and organization-specific application need separate review.
findings.product_implication: Separate evidence-backed incorporation, tax-account and charitable-status fields.

findings.finding: One or more persons may apply. Applicants can be individuals or organizations; the registry guide expressly lists a person, company, society or foreign corporation. An applicant is not automatically required to be a director. A society has no share capital. Its purposes must be lawful and may not include operating a business for profit or gain, although a business may support its purposes.
findings.section: ss2(1)-(2), 3, 13; registry guide Start a society steps3/5
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Keep applicants, directors and members as distinct records. Do not request share subscriptions or use a five-incorporator default from the former Act.

findings.finding: An approved reserved name and reservation number are prerequisites to society incorporation. Reservation normally lasts 56 days from reservation; the registrar may allow longer periods and extend a reservation. The current statute does not offer a business-company-style automatic numbered-name alternative.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Store approval and actual expiry from the name decision. Block an expired reservation; permit a verified extension instead of always forcing a new request.

findings.finding: Ordinary new-society incorporation is an online-only filing through Societies Online. WORK 01 SOC is a preparation worksheet, not a postal application. The current official forms catalogue lists it under preparatory papers and separately lists society transactions requiring mailed forms.
findings.section: WORK 01 SOC p1; official forms catalogue Societies / Gather information to prepare a filing
findings.confidence: High channel conclusion: explicit official worksheet plus catalogue and live portal; worksheet text retrieved via index
findings.unresolved: Live PDF/guide retrieval returned HTTP 502; no authorized portal walkthrough was performed.
findings.product_implication: Label downloads preparatory. Link to Societies Online. Do not display mail/fax destinations for an incorporation worksheet.
findings.short_quote: THIS IS AN ONLINE-ONLY PROCESS • DO NOT MAIL OR FAX

findings.finding: The society guide offers Service BC community internet terminals and professional filing assistance. The dedicated support page goes further: participating Service BC staff can submit forms/documents on behalf of a person with government-issued ID, a completed form and the filing fee; its published page excludes Vancouver, Surrey and Burnaby locations. This is an assisted service, not evidence that incorporation papers may be mailed directly to the registrar.
findings.section: Visit a Service BC location; Get assistance from a third party
findings.confidence: Medium: official indexed page, dated 2023-08-24, direct current retrieval unavailable
findings.unresolved: Confirm the chosen Service BC location currently supports new-society incorporation, how it handles the online certification, and which payment methods that location accepts. No incorporation-specific assisted processing SLA established.
findings.product_implication: Offer an assisted-filing option with a location/support link; retain online filing as the operative channel. Do not promise universal walk-in availability.

findings.finding: Societies Online requires a Basic BCeID; Business and Personal BCeID types are not accepted. Society access also uses a registry key created during incorporation. The official worksheet asks the filer to certify relevant knowledge and authorization; the worksheet has name, signature and date fields. A worksheet signature blank is not evidence that a wet-signed worksheet must be posted or uploaded.
findings.section: Get Started; Registry Key Help; WORK 01 SOC p2 sectionH
findings.confidence: High for account/key; medium for exact current electronic attestation mechanics
findings.unresolved: Current authenticated final-screen certification and payment screens were not traversed; do not invent e-signature vendor, witness or notarization requirements.
findings.product_implication: Collect the filer mandate and completion evidence. Keep Basic BCeID/registry key outside ordinary document/member metadata. Societyer sign-in does not confer registry filing authority.

findings.finding: The ordinary constitution contains only the name and purposes. Other governance terms belong in bylaws, except for the specifically permitted member-funded statement under s191(1). The constitution is part of the filed incorporation application.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Use a constrained constitution editor; do not put director lists, quorum, addresses, financial year or general dissolution clauses into its ordinary constitution fields.

findings.finding: Bylaws must cover membership admission/rights/classes/good standing; director election or appointment and relevant tenure terms; general-meeting quorum if greater than three, proxy permission, rules for authorized non-meeting voting; and activity/power restrictions. Prescribed Model Bylaws may be adopted wholly or partly, with modifications; inconsistent clauses have no effect.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Validate required subjects, persist original text and amendments, and record whether the society actually adopted the model. A draft worksheet is not operative bylaws.

findings.finding: Prepare primary/alternate contact email, approved name and number, applicant full names and contact/mailing information (including organization identifiers where applicable), purpose text/member-funded choice, full director names and physical service addresses, and BC registered-office mailing/delivery addresses. Choose unchanged Model Bylaws or upload custom bylaws. Official guidance allows English DOC, DOCX, PDF, RTF, TXT or WPS; the worksheet says uploaded bylaws are converted to PDF and the editable original should be retained.
findings.section: WORK 01 SOC pp1-2 sectionsA-I; registry guide Start a society steps2/5
findings.confidence: Medium-high: official current-linked worksheet; exact authenticated UI untested
findings.unresolved: Actual current portal upload limits and attestation interaction not inspected. Do not infer requirements from legacy FORM 01 SOC (JUL 2017).
findings.product_implication: Generate a field-complete preparation bundle and editable bylaws. Keep director consents internally; the verified filing inputs do not list consent uploads.

findings.finding: An ordinary society requires at least three directors, with at least one ordinarily resident in BC. A majority must neither receive nor be entitled to receive remuneration from the society under employment/service contracts, apart from remuneration for being directors. A member-funded society may have one director, has no BC-residency requirement and is exempt from that employment-majority rule. Model Bylaws nonetheless require three to eleven directors if adopted unchanged.
findings.section: ss40,41,197; Regulation Sch1 bylaw4.1 and s9.1
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.unresolved: Special regulatory exemption exists for First Nations Summit Society; custom/subtype cases require applicable-rule review.
findings.product_implication: Separate statutory minimum, subtype exception and adopted bylaw minimum. Member-funded status alone must not override an unchanged model three-director clause.

findings.finding: Directors must be individuals normally aged at least18 and meet bylaw qualifications. Ages16-17 are permitted only with enabling bylaws and a majority aged18+. Disqualifiers include incapacity findings/certificates, undischarged bankruptcy and convictions connected with promoting, forming or managing a corporation or unincorporated entity, or offences involving fraud. The five-year exception runs from the latest applicable statutory sentencing event: expiry of a period suspending the passing of sentence without a sentence being passed; imposition of a fine; end of imprisonment; or end of probation. Court, pardon and record-suspension exceptions also apply. Appointment is invalid without written consent or attendance without refusal at the appointing meeting.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Capture qualification declaration, bylaw-specific requirements and either written consent or the appointing-meeting evidence. Do not replace the conviction rule with a simplistic five-years-since-conviction checkbox.

findings.finding: A society must maintain a BC registered office with separate delivery and mailing address fields. Each director may use a residential address or an address where the director can ordinarily be served between9am and4pm local time Monday-Friday. The official worksheet rejects a PO box alone for delivery/director addresses and requires full names rather than initials.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Distinguish legal service address from private profile/home address and optional mailing address. Avoid requiring publication of a home address when a qualifying service address exists.

findings.finding: Regulation Schedule2 lists $100 incorporation, $30 name search/reservation (up to three proposed names), $40 annual report, $50 constitution/bylaw alteration and $100 priority service when offered. Baseline incorporation plus name is $130 CAD. The regulation permits an additional $1.50 operator charge plus applicable GST on that charge for certain electronic transactions. Professional-provider charges are separate.
findings.effective_or_version: BC Reg 216/2015; consolidation current to 2026-09-29; last amended 2022-07-04 by BC Reg 114/2022.
findings.product_implication: Display core government charges separately from optional priority/provider/operator charges. Treat $130 as baseline, not guaranteed checkout total.

findings.finding: The live Societies Online banner states five-business-day priority names/search and ten-business-day priority other filings. Older government society text advertises regular name processing7-14 days and priority1-2 days; indexed processing pages also conflict. No current ordinary online incorporation SLA was verified. Statutory incorporation occurs on filing, which requires registrar acceptance and inclusion in the register; clicking submit is not itself proof.
findings.section: Live priority-service banner; Act ss14(1),209(1); registry guide step4
findings.confidence: High current banner, unresolved normal queue and online incorporation turnaround
findings.unresolved: Recheck the Name Request live queue immediately before filing. Do not apply the generic ten-day manual-priority statement as a guaranteed online-incorporation turnaround.
findings.product_implication: Attach observed_at dates to service estimates. Completion depends on certificate/registry acceptance, not elapsed estimated days.

findings.finding: After incorporation the registrar issues a certificate with legal name, number, date and time; certified constitution, bylaws, statement of directors and registered office; and certified applicant-name/contact portion. Notice is published. The certificate and certified records must be preserved as legal records.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Promote preparation to incorporated only after recorded registry evidence. Store immutable originals, incorporation number and exact effective timestamp separately from workspace creation.

findings.finding: Member-funded status requires the prescribed constitutional statement and eligibility. It is prohibited for charities/other qualified donees, specified tax recipients, student societies, hospital societies and specified regulatory classes. Funding disqualification examines the two immediately preceding financial years: public donations, government funding or their combination exceeding the greater of $20,000 or10% of gross income. Statutory donor exclusions and the regulation COVID-relief exclusion matter.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Use a documented subtype eligibility review, not a self-description of private funding. Preserve measurement period, totals, exclusions and legal-review decision.

findings.finding: A member-funded society that becomes ineligible must immediately remove the statement; this compulsory alteration need not receive the usual special-resolution authorization. An existing ordinary society seeking to add member-funded status generally needs both a special resolution and a court declaration, followed by filing the entered order. Reduced public financial-disclosure and remuneration-note obligations do not remove members’ record rights or annual reporting.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Do not implement member-funded status as an editable checkbox after incorporation. Add annual eligibility review and an exceptional legal workflow for conversion.

findings.finding: AGM is required each calendar year except the incorporation year. Registrar extension must be requested by December31 and may authorize a date no later than March31 in the following year (or later prescribed date); the authorized meeting counts for the preceding year. Annual report is due within30 days after an AGM, including a deemed AGM. If no AGM occurs, report no AGM by January31 next year; after a missed authorized extension, within30 days of the authorized deadline.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Use calendar-year rules and explicit extension state. Distinguish due dates from reminders. Do not use a company-anniversary annual-report schedule.
findings.short_quote: within 30 days after an annual general meeting is held

findings.finding: An AGM may be deemed held when a resolution deals with every matter required by the Act and bylaws, including financial statements/auditor report, and all voting members consent in writing by the deadline. The deemed date is last consent or a specified later permitted date. An ordinary written resolution supported by two-thirds does not satisfy this AGM substitute.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Use a distinct unanimous-AGM-resolution workflow and retain all dated consents and presented financials.

findings.finding: Default written notice is at least14 days and at most60 days before a general meeting; bylaws may specify another minimum but no fewer than7 days. Notice goes to every member, not only voters. Include date/time, applicable location and exact special-resolution text, plus electronic participation/voting instructions if applicable. The >100-member alternative requires enabling bylaws and both email-to-known-addresses and specified newspaper/website publication.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Track recipient register snapshot, dispatch evidence, actual bylaw period and any waiver. Do not treat a website posting alone or workspace notification as universally sufficient legal notice.

findings.finding: Statutory general-meeting quorum is three voting members unless bylaws require more; if total voting members are fewer, all voting members form quorum. An adjourned-meeting reduced quorum is available only through enabling bylaws. Model bylaw3.7 sets the greater of three and10%; bylaws3.8-3.9 govern initial failure, resumed meeting and loss of quorum.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Keep quorum events across the meeting and across adjournments. Three,10% and adjourned attendees are different rules, not interchangeable defaults.

findings.finding: At a meeting, ordinary resolutions use a simple majority of votes cast, special resolutions at least two-thirds. Bylaws may increase the special threshold, except for statutory removal of a director. Ordinary written consent needs at least two-thirds of all voting members after distribution to all voting members; special written consent requires every voting member. Authorized delegate/mail/electronic ballot modes have separate bylaw-based mechanics.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Model decision body, mode, eligible electorate, votes cast versus all eligible, threshold and governing-clause version. Use exact integer fractions, not66.7% approximations.

findings.finding: Member proxy voting is prohibited unless bylaws permit it; appointment must be written, revocable and meet bylaw conditions. Unless bylaws say otherwise it is meeting-specific and the proxy holder must be a member. Directors cannot vote by proxy. Electronic member participation is generally allowed unless bylaws provide otherwise, with mutual participation and adequately disclosed voting intentions; an electronic meeting must be facilitated by the society.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Do not equate live electronic attendance with an asynchronous ballot. Store proxy instrument, scope and revocation, and suppress director-proxy controls.

findings.finding: Absent contrary bylaws, directors may meet at any location or electronically, on notice/manner convenient to them. A no-meeting directors’ resolution must be sent to every director; default consent is all directors, but bylaws may permit fewer and may prescribe a non-written consent method. Model bylaws require two days’ notice unless all agree to less, and majority director quorum. No universal statute-derived two-day notice or model quorum should be silently imposed on custom bylaws.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Persist the adopted board procedure. Director consent and member ordinary/special resolutions need separate evaluators.

findings.finding: Directors must present financial statements and any auditor report at each AGM. The covered period ends no more than six months before the AGM; statements must be director-approved and signed by at least one director before issue, with any auditor report attached. Audit is mandatory if bylaws or applicable regulation require one, not universally for all societies. Ordinary-society remuneration disclosures include all remunerated directors and staff/contractors at the regulation threshold of$75,000; member-funded s36 exemption applies.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Track financial period, board approval, signer and auditor status. Separate preparation/approval/presentation/filing; financial statements and minutes are retained, not annual-report attachments.

findings.finding: Pre-existing reporting societies carried Reporting Society Provisions into their bylaws at transition; confirm whether they were subsequently lawfully altered under s241.1. Where still applicable, Regulation Schedule3 requires an auditor, comparative statements subject to a stated reason exception, and financial statements/auditor report sent to members and auditor at least10 days before the AGM. This is a subtype/historical rule, not an ordinary-society default.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Capture legacy reporting status and filed transitioned bylaws before declaring audit or financial-distribution deadlines inapplicable.

findings.finding: Director/address changes must be filed promptly; AGM director changes may instead be in the annual report. Known statement errors require prompt correction. Registered-office changes may be filed separately or in an annual report and legally take effect the following day. Constitution/bylaw changes need special-resolution authorization and take effect on registry filing, not merely on voting or saving a draft.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Use proposed, authorized, submitted, accepted/effective states with different dates. Preserve both resolution and registrar-certified changed instrument.

findings.finding: Required records include certificate/certified instruments, court and official orders, director register (including appointment/cessation dates), consents/resignations, conflict disclosures, membership register by class, member meeting minutes and resolution texts, member written consents, financials/auditor reports, board minutes (with directors present and resolution texts), board consents and adequate accounting records. There is no share register for a society.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Build a society-specific records index and distinguish registry-original, legal internal, proposed draft and supporting evidence.

findings.finding: The statutory member register may contain only member names and provided contact information, organized by class where classes exist. Members have free inspection rights over s20(1) records. Board minutes/consents/accounting are generally inspectable unless bylaws restrict, but interest-disclosure portions remain available. Directors may inspect all s20 records. Non-members’ general inspection rights depend on bylaws and exclude the membership register.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Do not export private profile notes into the statutory register. A role matrix must coexist with a documented statutory record-request route and actual legal membership/directorship.

findings.finding: Directors may restrict members’ inspection of the membership register by resolution on a harmfulness assessment, but a compliant written purpose-limited request restores access. Information use is constrained. Requested copies generally must be supplied promptly and no later than14 days after request/payment; directors get copies free, members get one free current constitution/bylaws and latest financials. Ordinary societies must provide financial statements to other requesting persons under s28; member-funded societies are exempt from s28.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: Add request/decision/deadline/audit records and selective exports. Neither a blanket public viewer grant nor blanket member denial represents the Act.

findings.finding: Electronic records must be available for inspection at the BC registered office; directors may resolve to use another BC inspection location, with notice available at the office. Any form is allowed if inspectable/copyable, with reasonable measures for completeness, loss prevention, anti-falsification and reliable access. The ten-year rule permits ceasing to keep a record only if ten years have elapsed since creation/last alteration AND it is no longer relevant.
findings.effective_or_version: SBC 2015 c18; consolidation current to 2026-09-22. Retrieval date is not commencement date.
findings.product_implication: SharePoint/R2 storage can support the record book only with export, inspection access, version provenance and recovery. Do not configure universal ten-year deletion or infer a BC-only server-location mandate from these sections.

findings.finding: Society incorporation is separate from charitable registration and tax-account obligations. CRA describes registered charity and tax-law NPO as different categories; an NPO cannot issue official donation receipts. CRA’s BC society checklist asks for incorporation certificate and certified constitution, bylaws and statement of directors/office, including relevant alterations. A registry annual report is not a T3010, T1044 or tax return.
findings.section: Differences table; CRA application checklist / British Columbia Societies Act branch
findings.unresolved: Automatic BN/program-account creation for a new BC society was not established by current primary society guidance; verify the actual registry output and existing CRA account before requesting a new BN. Tax status and required accounts need accountant review.
findings.product_implication: Separate home incorporation, charity status, BN and program accounts; never infer charity or income-tax exemption from society incorporation.

findings.finding: The King’s Printer Licence v1.1 permits commercial/noncommercial use, copying and format adaptation of legislation and prescribed content, with accuracy/currentness, retained notices and the prescribed attribution/nonofficial disclaimer. Its definition expressly excludes fillable forms and other documents incorporating prescribed content. Societies Act s11(2) permits actual adoption/modification of model bylaw provisions. Government PDF/DOC presentation assets are not automatically covered by the statute-content licence.
findings.confidence: High: licence and statutory adoption provision inspected
findings.unresolved: General permission to redistribute/modify the WORK PDF or government DOC wrapper was not established.
findings.product_implication: Link official worksheets. If embedding statute/model text, follow the licence exactly and mark modifications accurately; do not brand custom drafts as government forms.

findings.finding: Unless a contrary intention appears, statutory time calculation uses the Interpretation Act. A period expressed as clear, at least or not less than has an extra day; at least14 days before ordinarily means14 intervening days, so the unadjusted latest sending date is15 days before the event. Holiday adjustment depends on counting direction; qualifying office closure has separate rules. Calendar-month calculations are not fixed day counts. Sunday is a statutory holiday; Saturday is not automatically one. Current s26 defines Pacific Time as UTC−7.
findings.effective_or_version: RSBC1996 c238; current to2026-09-22; commencement dates not separately isolated
findings.unresolved: Apply contrary-intention and office-closure rules to the particular transaction; obtain reviewed expected outputs before shipping a legal deadline calculator. No historical timezone backfill verified.
findings.product_implication: Store legal deadline wording, count direction, clear-day modifier, holiday source and local date/time separately from reminder lead time. Do not use naive meeting date minus14 or six months equals180 days.

findings.finding: The September 24, 2026 government guide directs most ordinary B.C. companies to Corporate Online. It also permits incorporation through the new BC Business Registry where no business-information changes are expected in the next six months, or where changes are limited to annual reports, business addresses, director names/addresses and basic alterations. Benefit companies use the new registry. Corporate Online is still operating while companies are invited to migrate in phases.
findings.section: Incorporate in B.C., step 5; modernization instructions; live incorporation entry screen
findings.effective_or_version: Guide updated 2026-09-24; migration guide 2026-02-17; live screen retrieved 2026-10-04
findings.unresolved: The new-service eligibility wording and transaction coverage can change during migration; no signed-in transaction was tested.
findings.product_implication: Store actual service and migration status per company. Maintain dated routing content and a current official link; do not globally replace Corporate Online or force all companies into it.

findings.finding: Regulation 30(2)(a) requires electronic submission of an incorporation application unless the registrar allows or requires another method. Form 1 is a preparation form and directs users not to mail it unless instructed by the registry. Current guidance sends applicants unable to file online to a law firm or registry agent to submit the completed information electronically. Service BC also offers assistance at participating locations; that is assisted filing, not proof of a routine mailed incorporation route.
findings.section: Reg. 30(2)(a); Form 1 header; current incorporation guide step 5
findings.effective_or_version: Consolidated to 2026-09-29; last amended 2026-01-12 by B.C. Reg. 3/2026; original regulation effective 2004-03-29.
findings.unresolved: A registrar-authorized paper exception remains legally possible, but its current approval criteria, accepted payment and processing time were not established. Confirm participation/charges before directing an applicant to a Service BC location.
findings.product_implication: Label Form 1 as official preparation/assisted-filing input. Do not provide a mail-submit button or a standard mail incorporation promise.
findings.short_quote: must be submitted for filing with the registrar in an electronic format

findings.finding: One may incorporate a numbered limited company without reserving a name. A named company requires the approved name and reservation number. The statutory normal reservation is 56 days from reservation, subject to a longer period or timely extension allowed by the registrar. Current government base name-request fee is CAD 30.
findings.section: ss. 10(3)(d), 22; Fees Schedule; current guide steps 1 and 5
findings.effective_or_version: Consolidated to 2026-09-22; this is the currency date, not a common commencement date for all provisions.
findings.product_implication: Collect name-request number, exact approved name and explicit expiry. Do not require a name search for a numbered company; calculate deadline from reservation/approval evidence, not workspace creation.

findings.finding: One or more persons can form the company. Each incorporator must agree to take at least one share in that incorporator's name. The agreement must identify each full name, signature line, date of signing and number of shares of each class and series taken, and every incorporator signs. The application lists all and only persons who signed both the agreement and articles. Director age rules must not be silently applied as an express incorporator rule.
findings.effective_or_version: Consolidated to 2026-09-22; this is the currency date, not a common commencement date for all provisions.
findings.product_implication: Create separate incorporator, subscriber, shareholder and director records. Check signatures and class/series quantities across both operative documents and filed data.

findings.finding: The incorporation agreement and articles are signed operative internal records. The incorporation application is submitted to the registry and includes the notice of articles and the completing-party statement. The notice identifies directors, offices and authorized share structure; it does not replace the detailed articles. Articles and agreement remain with the company, rather than being routinely uploaded/filed with the incorporation application.
findings.effective_or_version: Consolidated to 2026-09-22; this is the currency date, not a common commencement date for all provisions.
findings.product_implication: Give each document its own document type, status, version and signature evidence. Never label the existing text worksheet as articles, agreement or filed application.

findings.finding: Articles establish company rules, use numbered/lettered paragraphs, contain any business/power restrictions and all special rights/restrictions attached to each share class or series, and identify the company. All incorporators sign the initial articles. All or part of the statutory Table 1 may be adopted by reference or restatement, with or without changes. Table 1 is not automatically imposed on every new company. Adoption by reference generally tracks later Table 1 amendments unless the articles provide otherwise; altered provisions have a statutory exception.
findings.effective_or_version: Consolidated to 2026-09-22; this is the currency date, not a common commencement date for all provisions.
findings.product_implication: Record the actual adopted articles, mode of Table 1 adoption, incorporated version and amendments. Obtain legal review for custom share rights, transfer controls, founders/investors and special subtypes.

findings.finding: The individual completing party must examine the signed agreement and articles, verify endorsements, include the correct incorporators and complete the statutory statement before submission. After incorporation, the originally signed documents go to the records office by delivery or registered mail as specified in section 15. The live portal requires confirmation of the signed preparatory documents. General electronic-signature legislation supports electronic signatures and original retention subject to consent, integrity, accessibility and retention requirements; it does not remove the completing party's duties or override a specifically required delivery method.
findings.section: BCA s. 15; Electronic Transactions Act ss. 2, 4, 8-11; Corporate Online confirmation

findings.finding: The notice of articles identifies each class/series and kind, maximum authorized shares or unlimited status, par value where applicable or no-par status, and whether special rights/restrictions exist. The articles contain those rights. Subscription in the incorporation agreement is distinct from actual share issuance. Directors must authorize issuance and applicable price consistent with the articles, and shares cannot issue until fully paid through money, qualifying property or past services; the subscriber's own debt instrument and future services are not qualifying payment under section 64.

findings.finding: An ordinary company requires at least one director; a public company requires at least three. Each director must be a qualified individual aged at least 18, with disqualification rules for incapacity, undischarged bankruptcy and specified convictions, subject to statutory exceptions. The Act has no general Canadian or B.C. director-residency requirement. A director need not hold shares unless the articles require them. A community contribution company separately requires at least three directors.

findings.finding: A first director is validly designated through the statutory incorporator/articles-signature route or required consent route in section 121. Written consent can be given before or after designation; section 123 also recognizes conduct showing consent. Election/appointment rules in section 122 add attendance/non-refusal situations. Written consent evidence is a sensible product requirement but is not the sole legally possible method in every case.

findings.finding: Both registered and records offices must be in B.C.; they may be the same place. Each has a mailing and delivery address. A delivery location must be uniquely identifiable and publicly accessible during statutory business hours, and cannot be a post office box. For a director, the director chooses a qualifying service office or residence, with delivery and, if different, mailing address. A director need not expose a home address where a valid service address is selected.

For starred electronic fees, the schedule allows an additional CAD 1.50 operator fee plus applicable GST. Government fee guidance says GST does not apply to registry service fees themselves. Third-party professional/agent charges are separate.

findings.finding: The standard completion package includes certificate of incorporation, certified incorporation application, certified notice of articles and a cover sheet with incorporation number and business number, delivered through the selected notification method. The company arises on its legal incorporation time, not when a Societyer workspace or checklist is created. Section 18 makes the register's incorporation notation conclusive evidence despite failures in incorporation prerequisites; product wording should not declare an existing company nonexistent merely because a signed preparation document is missing.

findings.finding: After incorporation, complete initial board/shareholder decisions appropriate to the company: authorize and pay for share issuance, establish banking/signing authority, set financial year, appoint officers where desired, appoint the first auditor or obtain the applicable unanimous waiver, and create the directors, securities and applicable transparency registers. Sections 42-44 govern minute-book records, including operative articles/agreement, certificate, consents, minutes/resolutions and financial material. Not all suggested organizational actions are individually mandatory in every company.

findings.finding: The regulation expressly permits electronic corporate records. Section 43(2) allows records elsewhere if inspection and copying remain available at the B.C. records office through electronic technology; separate securities-register requirements apply. Records must remain complete, accessible and protected against loss/falsification. The statutory seven-year rule for moving specified older records, and the seven-year accounting-record retention requirement, do not authorize deletion of all corporate documents after seven years.

findings.finding: Public status, benefit status, ULC status and community-contribution status have separate legal consequences and should not be a single undifferentiated company mode. Public companies have at least three directors, longer minimum meeting notice and securities-law overlays. Benefit companies require the benefit statement/provision, modified directors' duties and annual benefit report, and currently use the new registry. ULCs impose exceptional shareholder liability and use different naming/documents and a CAD 1,000 fee. Community contribution companies have community-purpose and distribution constraints, at least three directors, a community-contribution report and no section 200 financial-statement waiver.

findings.finding: A general meeting notice must satisfy section 169 and the prescribed minimum, and cannot be sent more than two months before the meeting. For a private company, articles may set a period of at least ten days; otherwise the default is 21 days. For a public company the minimum is 21 days or a longer articles period. The articles may set different periods for different subjects. Notice waivers and special-resolution notice content require separate handling; electronic/hybrid notice must explain participation and voting.

findings.finding: Section 172 first uses the articles quorum; if none, it is two shareholders entitled to vote, present personally or by proxy. If fewer eligible shareholders exist than the applicable quorum, all eligible shareholders suffice. One voting shareholder may constitute the meeting. Table 1 article 8.2 instead requires two qualifying persons representing at least one-twentieth of issued shares entitled to vote, with a sole-shareholder rule and separate adjournment provisions. The Table 1 percentage applies only when adopted.
findings.effective_or_version: Consolidated to 2026-09-22; this is the currency date, not a common commencement date for all provisions.
findings.product_implication: Model headcount and represented voting-share thresholds separately, including sole-holder and adjournment rules. Do not label two people plus five percent as the universal statutory quorum.

findings.finding: At a meeting, an ordinary resolution is a simple majority of votes cast. A special resolution uses the applicable special majority and proper notice of intention. The special majority is normally two-thirds unless the articles specify a fraction between two-thirds and three-quarters; pre-existing companies can have a three-quarters statutory baseline. Consent ordinary resolutions are different: after circulation to every shareholder entitled to vote, signatures representing at least the applicable special majority of eligible votes suffice. A written special resolution requires all shareholders entitled to vote on it. Statutory unanimous resolutions can require all shareholders including otherwise non-voting shareholders for designated matters.

findings.product_implication: Separate resolution kind, meeting/consent method, denominator (cast versus eligible), class/series electorate and threshold. A generic majority/unanimous toggle is inadequate. Store the company's legacy status and actual articles.

findings.finding: Subject to the Act and share rights/articles, voting is one vote per share and shareholders may vote by proxy. Default meeting methods distinguish remote participation, polls and show of hands. Table 1 article 9.1 assigns one vote per eligible attendee on a show of hands and one per share on a poll, subject to rights restrictions. Its private-company proxy provisions set instrument, deposit and revocation rules, and ordinarily require a shareholder proxy-holder with exceptions. Poll ballots and voted proxies must be retained for at least three months, with inspection rights for entitled shareholders/proxy-holders.
findings.effective_or_version: Consolidated to 2026-09-22; this is the currency date, not a common commencement date for all provisions.
findings.product_implication: Voting power follows securities rights and poll method, not Societyer Member/Director roles or one-account-one-vote. Capture proxies, revocations, authority, exclusions and retention.

findings.finding: Subject to the articles, shareholders and directors may participate through communications media if all participants can participate in the meeting. A company must facilitate the chosen electronic meeting; a physical meeting does not universally create an obligation to supply remote facilities. Fully electronic general meetings are exempt from the physical B.C.-location rule; the physical location of a hybrid meeting remains subject to section 166. Merely publishing a recording or email poll does not establish compliant meeting participation.
findings.effective_or_version: Consolidated to 2026-09-22; this is the currency date, not a common commencement date for all provisions.
findings.product_implication: Record meeting mode, applicable articles, participation/voting instructions and evidence of usable facilities. Do not treat asynchronous written resolutions as virtual meetings.

findings.finding: Section 140 permits written director resolutions with consent of each director entitled to vote, with a specific interested-transaction rule and an alternative manner if the Act/articles permit it. A sole director can constitute a meeting. Table 1 provides majority votes, no chair casting vote, a board-set quorum or otherwise a majority, and reasonable notice of extraordinary meetings rather than a fixed universal number of days. Under section 149 an interested director normally cannot vote to approve that contract, but can count toward quorum unless articles say otherwise; if all directors are interested the Act permits them to vote.

findings.finding: The first AGM is due within 18 months after recognition. Afterwards it is required in each calendar year and no later than 15 months after the preceding calendar year's annual reference date. All shareholders entitled to vote at that AGM may unanimously defer, consent to all required business or waive the meeting under section 182, with the required selection of an appropriate annual reference date. The registrar can grant an extension in the statutory circumstances. Waiving an AGM does not remove the separate annual-report filing requirement.

findings.finding: For companies subject to Part 6, directors generally produce/publish prescribed financial statements by the annual reference date and may need interim statements if publication is more than six months after the current financial year began. There is an exception before the first financial year ends. Statements require board approval and at least one director's confirming signature. At an AGM the required statements and auditor report are placed before shareholders and copies supplied on request; shareholder requests made within six months after annual reference date must be answered promptly. Section 185 does not create a universal 21-day pre-AGM financial-delivery deadline for an ordinary private B.C. company. Financial-production waiver, GAAP waiver and auditor waiver are separate unanimous-all-shareholder decisions with different scope; auditor waiver lasts only one financial year. Public/securities and CCC rules differ.

findings.product_implication: Do not import federal financial deadlines or treat no auditor as no statements. Track three distinct waivers, financial year, publication and board approval, with subtype exclusions and accountant/legal review.

findings.finding: A home B.C. company files its annual report within two months after each anniversary of recognition, reporting information current to that anniversary. The current statutory annual-report fee is CAD 43.39. A change in directors or a director's prescribed address requires filing within 15 days. Registered/records-office address changes are authorized under articles or by directors when silent, filed under section 35, and normally legally take effect at the beginning of the day after filing or an allowed later date; this is not a universal 15-day address-change rule.

findings.finding: Part 4.1 requires an internal transparency register for applicable private B.C. companies. It excludes reporting issuers/equivalents, designated-exchange companies and prescribed classes under Regulation 47. Significant-individual analysis includes at least 25 percent of issued shares or voting rights, direct/beneficial/indirect interests and control over appointment/removal of a majority of directors, plus joint/control arrangements; a simple cap-table percentage test is incomplete. Current prescribed exemptions include specified public-company subsidiaries, financial/government/municipal/school classes, wholly Indigenous-nation-owned companies and wholly professional-LLP-owned companies.

findings.finding: Required significant-individual information includes name, birth date, last known address, citizenship/permanent-resident or citizenship-country details, Canadian tax-residency status, dates becoming/ceasing significant and the basis of significance. The company takes reasonable steps and records unsuccessful efforts or absence of significant individuals. Annual confirmation falls in the period from recognition anniversary through two months later; new/different information is entered within 30 days of awareness; status-entry notices go to the individual within ten days. The register is not generally open to shareholders or the public merely because they have that status.

findings.finding: Directors may set distinct notice/voting record dates within statutory bounds. With no set date, the default for notice and voting is 5 p.m. on the day before the first notice is sent, or the beginning of the meeting if no notice is sent. Notices/records may use a method agreed with the recipient, an applicable articles method or the statutory methods; the regulation recognizes email to an address supplied for the relevant records. A current workspace email is not automatically evidence of every shareholder's authorized notice address.

The defined term is not equivalent to citizenship alone or a mailing address. Prescribed sectors and other Acts requiring Canadian control can require a resident-Canadian majority. For that special regime, a one/two-director corporation needs one resident Canadian; s. 105(4) provides a holding-company exception where Canadian revenue is below 5% of consolidated gross revenue.
