findings.product_implication: Create linked execution tasks and share-issue evidence rather than auto-issuing shares when users are invited.

findings.finding: Corporations Canada publishes an actual CBCA business-corporation model, distinct from its NFP tools. It contains adjustable quorum/casting-vote choices, a 48-hour board-notice clause and bylaw adoption/confirmation signature blocks. These are model choices and do not establish statutory defaults or completed adoption.
findings.unresolved: Commercial redistribution/adaptation rights for ISED nonstatutory model remain unverified; current legal suitability needs review.
findings.product_implication: Add an official-model inventory entry with review state; do not silently install its blanks or notice clause as law.

findings.finding: Subject to articles/bylaws/unanimous shareholder agreement, directors make bylaws by resolution. Shareholders at the next meeting may confirm, amend or reject by ordinary resolution. Failure to submit or rejection ends effectiveness under the statute.
findings.effective_or_version: CBCA consolidation current to 2026-09-21; Act last amended 2026-03-26; individual provision commencement not inferred from consolidation date
findings.product_implication: Track board adoption date and next shareholder-confirmation task; keeping a draft in storage is not adoption.

findings.finding: Maintain articles/bylaws, unanimous shareholder agreements, shareholder minutes/resolutions, director notices, securities register and adequate board/accounting records. Accounting records generally require six years after the related financial year. Section 20(5.1) allows covered records outside Canada subject to statutory Canadian inspection access; it should not be assumed to override separate ISC or securities-location provisions.
findings.effective_or_version: CBCA consolidation current to 2026-09-21; Act last amended 2026-03-26; individual provision commencement not inferred from consolidation date
findings.product_implication: Specify accessible statutory record locations and export/inspection workflows independently of storage-provider marketing; review each register’s location rules.

findings.finding: The federal, BC and Ontario incorporation pathways automatically generate a CRA business number and corporation income-tax program account (RC). Additional program accounts and authorized online account access have their own requirements. Certificate, filed articles and registry confirmation remain separate evidence from tax registration.
findings.product_implication: Capture BN/RC evidence when received; do not assume all GST/HST/payroll accounts or CRA access are established.

findings.finding: The annual registry return is due within 60 days after the incorporation/amalgamation/continuance anniversary, beginning after the year of that event; it is not an income-tax return. Current online fee is $12. AGM and financial disclosure run on different statutory clocks.
findings.product_implication: Keep anniversary, fiscal year end, last AGM and tax year end as independent event fields.

findings.finding: Federal incorporation does not remove provincial registration duties. The federal service describes coordinated registration during incorporation for Ontario, Nova Scotia and Newfoundland and Labrador, with other provincial pathways linked after incorporation. Confirm completion in the destination registry rather than inferring it from a checkbox.
findings.section: Provincial registration during and after incorporation
findings.product_implication: Use multiple registration records per legal entity, retaining home statute and each provincial activity/registration trigger.

findings.entity: Federal CBCA corporation carrying on business in BC
findings.finding: BC generally requires registration within two months after beginning to carry on business. The statute includes BC address/phone listings, resident agents, offices and warehouses among deeming rules, with specific exceptions. A federal corporation does not reserve its name in BC for this registration.
findings.product_implication: Record the factual BC activity start date and exemption assessment; do not substitute federal incorporation date.

findings.entity: Federal CBCA corporation carrying on business in BC
findings.finding: Corporate Online registration costs $350. Regulation 30(2)(k) requires electronic filing unless the registrar allows or requires otherwise. The current Form 33 table limits paper submission to LLCs; an ordinary CBCA corporation’s paper exception is not verified. Professional assistance can support electronic filing and is not itself an offline route. An attorney is generally required unless charter head office is in BC; eligible attorney is a BC-resident individual or BC company receiving legal notices, not necessarily retained legal counsel.
findings.section: Form 33 entry and forms instructions; Business Corporations Regulation s. 30(2)(k); BCBCA ss. 376, 386, 388
findings.effective_or_version: Guide updated 2026-09-24; forms table retrieved 2026-10-04; Act current 2026-09-22; Regulation current 2026-09-29, last amended 2026-01-12
findings.unresolved: Whether the registrar permits a paper-filing exception for an ordinary CBCA corporation, and the applicable package, delivery/payment instructions and processing standard, remain unresolved. The LLC paper option does not establish such an exception.
findings.product_implication: Collect head-office/attorney address evidence and registration certificate. Offer verified electronic filing or professional assistance; do not present Form 33 as a general paper route for CBCA corporations or infer BC authority from federal portal access.

findings.entity: Federal CBCA corporation registered in BC
findings.finding: The BC extra-provincial annual report is due within two months after its BC registration anniversary; the guide lists $43.39. This is additional to the federal return, with a different anniversary. Registration outputs include certificate, statement and cover information.
findings.product_implication: Add a separate BC EP annual obligation and preserve its certificate/number/registration date.

findings.topic: Ontario incorporation and official mail route
findings.finding: Ontario’s effective 2025 notice expressly permits direct online incorporation through its Business Registry/ServiceOntario account or mail using Form 5351; an intermediary is optional. All incorporators sign. Mail articles must be computer-completed, printed and submitted as one set, with the required payment and email information.
findings.product_implication: Ontario can support an explicitly verified paper preparation path. Keep professional fees outside the government fee.

findings.finding: The official indexed service table lists $300 incorporation both online (immediate) and by mail (15 business days). Initial returns and notices of change are free, with immediate online or 15-business-day mail service. The direct page was inaccessible, so the table must be reconfirmed before release.
findings.effective_or_version: Official indexed page accessed 2026-10-04; page date unverified
findings.unresolved: Re-open the live government fees table before shipping automated fee/timing promises.
findings.product_implication: Use provisional dated source-backed figures, not third-party $360 paper claims.

findings.finding: Named incorporation requires an Ontario-biased Nuans search dated no more than 90 days before submission; numbered incorporation does not. Enter its report reference/name/date and retain the report rather than attach it. Articles specify Ontario street registered office, incorporators/directors and customized share, restriction and other clauses.
findings.product_implication: Do not reuse the federal integrated-name-search workflow or assume a worksheet constitutes Ontario articles.

findings.finding: A first director who is not an incorporator completes Form 5260, giving name, service address, corporation name and signature. Retain it at the registered office; do not submit it unless requested. This form explicitly applies to OBCA and ONCA.
findings.product_implication: Add an internal signed-consent document task independent of portal entry and workspace invitation.

findings.finding: Mail to Business Registry Services Branch, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery and Procurement, 393 University Avenue, Suite 200, Toronto ON M5G 2M2. Pay by cheque to Minister of Finance as instructed. Successful incorporation emails a certificate, endorsed articles and receipt; defects can change the effective date.
findings.product_implication: Retain signed articles and supporting consents/Nuans; use the certificate date to activate the home registration.

findings.finding: The Companies Information Act initial return is due within 60 days of incorporation, amalgamation or continuance. Changes covered by the Act require notice within 15 days. Administrative email/NAICS updates also need maintenance but are distinguished in the notice from statutory return information.
findings.product_implication: Home trigger must name the applicable home event; do not use one ambiguous incorporationDate for every registration.
findings.short_quote: within 60 days after the date of incorporation, amalgamation or continuation

findings.entity: Federal or other Canadian corporation carrying on business in Ontario
findings.finding: The initial extra-provincial information return is due within 60 days of beginning business in Ontario, and covered changes within 15 days. Form 5286 applies. A domestic extra-provincial corporation is distinct from a foreign corporation incorporated outside Canada requiring an extra-provincial licence.
findings.section: CIA ss. 3, 4; notice scope; initial return requirements
findings.product_implication: Fix EP initial-return anchor to Ontario business commencement, not registration or original incorporation. Keep Canada/foreign licence classification explicit.
findings.short_quote: within 60 days after the date the corporation begins to carry on business in Ontario

findings.finding: The Ontario notice permits online or mail initial return/change without a government fee. It asks for legal identity and jurisdiction, head office, Ontario business start/cessation, principal Ontario location and chief Ontario manager if any. Agent-for-service and prior licence requirements apply to particular foreign licensed corporations, not every CBCA entity.
findings.product_implication: Collect provincial facts separately and retain the filed return/OCN confirmation. Coordinated federal data transfer still needs completion evidence.

findings.topic: Ontario annual return scope and date
findings.entity: Ontario home corporations and licensed foreign corporations
findings.finding: The 2025 annual-return notice covers Ontario corporations under named Ontario Acts and foreign corporations with an Extra-Provincial Corporations Act licence. It requires the return within six months of taxation year end, directly to Ontario rather than with the CRA return. An ordinary federal CBCA corporation registered in Ontario is not in that listed annual-return class.
findings.product_implication: Do not add an Ontario annual-return reminder merely because a CBCA entity has an Ontario extra-provincial registration.

findings.finding: Official indexed OBCA text shows that certain non-offering written ordinary resolutions may pass with holders of at least a majority of entitled shares, coupled with notice to non-signers within ten business days. This is materially different from CBCA unanimity. Ontario repealed the director Canadian-residency quota in 2021; current form instructions still ask for resident-Canadian status as a data item.
findings.confidence: Official indexed law; direct consolidated text inaccessible
findings.unresolved: Obtain accessible current full OBCA consolidation and validate all exceptions, articles/USA higher thresholds and remaining meeting rules before enabling a reviewed Ontario governance pack.
findings.product_implication: Do not derive complete Ontario governance from CBCA or infer a quota from the residency checkbox.

findings.finding: Ontario’s beneficial-ownership requirements began 2023-01-01 and concern internal records made available to specified authorities. They should not be represented as the federal CBCA public ISC filing regime.
findings.unresolved: Validate current OBCA ss. 1.1, 140.2-140.3 and exceptions against full accessible consolidation before implementing Ontario control-register deadlines.
findings.product_implication: Keep Ontario ownership-register configuration separate from federal public/private submission fields.

findings.finding: Sites.Selected targets site collections; Lists.SelectedOperations.Selected targets lists/libraries; ListItems.SelectedOperations.Selected and Files.SelectedOperations.Selected narrow access further. All support delegated and application modes.
findings.product_implication: Prefer one approved site or library per workspace; test exact endpoint compatibility before selecting the narrowest scope.

findings.finding: Selected access requires Entra consent, an explicit resource permission assignment, and a Graph token acquired with the corresponding delegated scope or application permission. A consented app initially has no selected-resource access.
findings.product_implication: Record consent status and resource permission IDs separately. Keep provisioning authority separate from runtime write authority.
findings.short_quote: If any of the three steps are missed, the application doesn't have access.

findings.finding: Delegated access intersects application permissions with the signed-in user’s existing resource rights. App-only checks the application grant without intersecting any Societyer user’s SharePoint ACL.
findings.product_implication: Choose and disclose the access model. A Societyer role alone never establishes a Microsoft user permission; app-only proxy must enforce Societyer record policy.

findings.finding: Application assignments below the site collection level break permission inheritance. Grant-management authority varies by level; site permission assignment requires Sites.FullControl.All.
findings.section: How Selected scopes work; What permissions do I need to manage permissions?
findings.unresolved: Selected scope and resource grant combinations can overlap; revocation must enumerate actual active grants.
findings.product_implication: Prefer dedicated resources. Do not leave tenant-wide provisioning privileges on the document runtime app.

findings.finding: Client credentials support certificates or federated credentials as higher-assurance alternatives to shared secrets. Tokens target the resource, such as Microsoft Graph with its .default scope.
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.unresolved: The Societyer hosting platform’s workload identity capability and the company’s credential policy are not established.
findings.product_implication: Use a certificate with managed rotation, or workload identity federation only where the hosting platform supplies a supported trusted issuer. Store references to credentials, never credential material in workspace records.

findings.finding: App-only Graph application permissions require administrator consent. Graph calls use an access token issued for Graph; existing sign-in/profile sessions do not themselves authorize Graph documents.
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.product_implication: Keep Clerk sign-in and the Microsoft storage connection separate. Record tenant ID, client ID and consented permissions for the storage connection.

findings.finding: Microsoft’s app-only guidance names Entra applications as preferred; Azure ACS app-only stops working from 2 April 2026.
findings.product_implication: Implement Microsoft Graph/Entra; reject old appregnew.aspx/ACS recipes for a new connector.

findings.finding: A driveItem ID persists through rename and move operations within its drive; a path changes when the item is renamed or moved.
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.product_implication: Store tenantId, siteId, listId, driveId and itemId; treat webUrl/path/name as mutable presentation data.

findings.finding: The move-item PATCH cannot move an item between drives. It supports If-Match and returns 412 for a mismatched eTag.
findings.product_implication: Treat cross-library/site moves as a migration with new provider identifiers, integrity checks and explicit mapping updates. Do not silently update a stored URL.

findings.finding: Single-call content upload supports files up to 250 MB. Replacing contents protected with a sensitivity label is unsupported with app-only authentication; Microsoft directs callers to delegated permissions.
findings.product_implication: Use upload sessions for larger files. Include labeled Office files in the POC and select a compatible access mode; never strip labels to force an upload.

findings.finding: Upload-session fragments must be sequential, each request under 60 MiB and normal fragment sizes divisible by 320 KiB. Sessions expire, expose nextExpectedRanges, and support If-Match preconditions.
findings.section: Request headers; Upload bytes; Resume upload
findings.unresolved: Test concurrent external edits during a session; do not claim an atomic cross-system database/storage transaction.
findings.product_implication: Use a tested 10 MiB fragment size, resumable job state and explicit conflict handling; protect preauthenticated upload URLs as credentials.

findings.finding: The preauthenticated download URL is short-lived (approximately one hour), must not be cached, and may remain usable after the user’s file permissions are removed.
findings.product_implication: Stream or proxy sensitive downloads through a server route that rechecks each new request and keeps the provider URL private. A redirect exposes the underlying bearer URL; a Societyer wrapper expiry cannot shorten Graph’s service-controlled lifetime. Do not promise instant revocation of already-issued URLs or downloaded content.

findings.finding: Graph returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After; use that delay, or exponential backoff when absent. Requests inside a batch can be throttled separately.
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.product_implication: Apply bounded retries with jitter, per-tenant queues and idempotent finalization. Use change tracking instead of frequent full scans.

findings.finding: driveItem delta supports paginated nextLink and deltaLink state. A stale or invalid synchronization token can cause HTTP 410 and require a fresh enumeration.
findings.product_implication: Persist opaque cursors per connection/drive. Reconcile deletions, duplicates and external renames; quarantine conflicts instead of interpreting an empty failed sync as mass deletion.

findings.finding: driveItem and SharePoint list subscriptions have a maximum 42,300-minute lifetime; documented average latency is under a minute but maximum latency can be six hours.
findings.unresolved: Verify selected-scope support for the chosen list/drive subscription in the POC; never widen to tenant-wide access merely to make discovery convenient.
findings.product_implication: Renew subscriptions ahead of expiry and supplement notifications with delta reconciliation. Notifications cannot be the authorization freshness boundary.

findings.finding: Graph represents a version with its own opaque ID, size, modification metadata and publication facet; it exposes version download and restore operations.
findings.product_implication: Map Societyer logical version IDs to driveId/itemId/versionId. Export each required historical version separately and preserve adopted-from relationships.

findings.finding: Automatic and manual count/age version policies can differ by organization, site and library. Versions trimmed by limits or jobs bypass the recycle bin. Retention policies/holds can suspend trimming.
findings.section: Types of version limits; Version storage behavior
findings.product_implication: Inspect the selected library’s actual settings. A native version ID is not a perpetual record-retention guarantee; approved records need their own retention design.

findings.finding: Retention may preserve a copy in the Preservation Hold library while the user edits/deletes the visible item. Locked record and regulatory-record settings can block edit/deletion. Retention policies or eDiscovery holds can override ordinary version limits.
findings.section: How retention works; How retention works with document versions
findings.unresolved: The tenant’s actual retention labels, holds, licensing and legal authorization are unknown.
findings.product_implication: Represent deletion-requested, hidden, retained and permanently-purged as distinct states. Preserve compliance-managed copies and surface provider refusal without bypass attempts.

findings.finding: First- and second-stage recycle bins share 93 days from original deletion, subject to quota purging or administrator deletion. Second-stage recovery requires appropriate administrator access.
findings.section: How long are deleted items kept?
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.product_implication: Offer a documented recovery workflow, not a promised extra 93 days after emptying the first bin. Keep independent backup/restore objectives.

findings.finding: Microsoft describes document-library Files Restore over the preceding 30 days and service point-in-time recovery support over a 14-day window.
findings.section: Files Restore; Point in Time Restore
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.unresolved: Confirm applicable recovery scope and support eligibility with the administrator; no live restore was attempted.
findings.product_implication: Distinguish native recent recovery from an independently managed backup and a long-term legal archive.

findings.finding: Audit Standard generally retains 180 days. One-year retention for SharePoint audit events under Audit Premium depends on the generating user’s eligible license; longer retention needs appropriate policies/add-ons.
findings.section: Default audit log retention policy; License requirements
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.product_implication: Retain Societyer’s own action/audit trail and export permitted vendor evidence on an agreed schedule; do not advertise universal one-year Microsoft audit history.

findings.finding: Audit Standard is included in Business Basic/Standard/Premium. SharePoint retention policies have different entitlements (including Business Premium, E3/E5 or SharePoint Plan 2); advanced record/default-label features require higher entitlements. Shared-site owners/members may need qualifying licenses.
findings.section: Audit Standard; Data Lifecycle & Records Management; Which users need a license?
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.unresolved: Publishing labels, default library labels, record declaration, adaptive scopes and eDiscovery are distinct licensing decisions.
findings.product_implication: Price the exact controls, not just storage. Validate all benefiting users and policy mechanisms with the company administrator.

findings.finding: Most eligible paid plans pool 1 TB plus 10 GB per license; frontline/education and other listed exceptions apply. The site maximum is 25 TB, file upload maximum 250 GB, decoded path maximum 400 characters. The pool excludes users’ separate OneDrive allocations.
findings.section: Limits by plan; File size and file path length
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.product_implication: Budget current content, historical versions, first-stage recycle bin and retained copies. Validate path/size before uploads; do not equate marketing’s per-user OneDrive terabyte with pooled SharePoint.

findings.finding: External sharing is controlled at organization and site levels and can create guest collaboration access. Available modes include authenticated guests and, if enabled, links that do not require sign-in.
findings.section: External sharing settings; What external users can do
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.unresolved: The 1stform tenant’s guest settings, group membership and existing sharing links have not been inspected.
findings.product_implication: Default Societyer-managed governance libraries to authenticated sharing. Native SharePoint grants and links remain independent of Societyer membership unless explicitly reconciled.

findings.finding: Current MCA SharePoint terms exempt external users invited to site collections through Share-by-Mail from User SLs for the listed plans; extra storage is required beyond the subscribed allowance.
findings.effective_or_version: Current displayed Microsoft Customer Agreement program terms; customer contract version must be checked
findings.unresolved: Customer’s actual agreement program/renewal terms and external-user definitions require administrator/licensing review.
findings.product_implication: Confirm whether each proposed external-user access path qualifies. Do not assume arbitrary app-only SaaS users are licensed as Microsoft guests.

findings.finding: Universal Online Services terms require appropriate licenses and state that pooling connections or reducing direct/indirect users through software does not reduce license requirements.
findings.effective_or_version: Current displayed MCA terms; customer purchase/renewal terms may differ
findings.product_implication: Treat app-only proxy access as an access architecture, not a license-saving mechanism. Validate before selling shared company-tenant storage to third-party customers.

findings.finding: The Canadian SharePoint page displays Business Basic at CAD 9.50 per user/month with Teams or CAD 7.30 without Teams, both paid yearly plus taxes.
findings.effective_or_version: Prices displayed on retrieval 2026-10-04; annual subscription, before taxes
findings.unresolved: Promotions, nonprofit eligibility, reseller agreements, annual commitments and required advanced controls can change the payable amount.
findings.product_implication: Use actual tenant contract and spare capacity for incremental cost. The retrieved page did not establish a current standalone Plan 1 Canadian quote.

findings.finding: Standard Graph CRUD/admin APIs within usage thresholds are included with the user license without additional API charges; metered APIs are a separate category.
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.product_implication: For normal document CRUD, budget licensing, hosting and administration rather than a generic Graph per-request tariff.

findings.finding: The current metered list charges assignSensitivityLabel USD 0.00185 per call; it requires billing setup.
findings.product_implication: Do not include label assignment automation in a zero-additional-API-cost claim.

findings.finding: Published list pricing is USD 0.15 per GB/month of protected content, with billable protection definitions beyond just current visible file bytes.
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.product_implication: Quote backup separately. A 1,000-GB protected volume has a USD 150/month list-price component before taxes/contract conversion; calculate actual protected footprint.

findings.finding: SharePoint uses TLS in transit and per-file/chunk AES-256 encryption at rest with tenant-isolated keys.
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.product_implication: Document service encryption accurately; separately decide whether customer-managed keys, sensitivity protection or client encryption are required. Encryption does not itself enforce Societyer roles.

findings.finding: Microsoft’s current data-residency terms include Canada for in-scope SharePoint site content/files when the tenant meets the specified provisioning conditions.
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.unresolved: The 1stform hostname does not establish tenant UUID, geography, owner, license or SharePoint data location; app database/cache/backups need their own location review.
findings.product_implication: A Canadian tenant can be a candidate for Canada-at-rest requirements. Obtain tenant-admin evidence of actual provisioning and contractual commitment.

findings.finding: SharePoint data-residency documentation distinguishes Product Terms commitments, Advanced Data Residency and Multi-Geo, with separate eligibility/configuration requirements.
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.product_implication: Do not infer the entire Societyer application is Canada-resident from a SharePoint library. Record verified scope, regions, migration status and evidence date.

findings.finding: Standard: USD 0.015/GB-month, 4.50/million Class A, 0.36/million Class B; Standard free allowances are 10 GB-month, 1 million A and 10 million B monthly. IA: 0.01/GB-month, 9.00/million A, 0.90/million B and 0.01/GB retrieval. Direct egress is free.
findings.effective_or_version: Page updated 2026-10-01; current retrieved prices in USD
findings.unresolved: The free allowance is shared across account usage, not a free allocation for every workspace.
findings.product_implication: Include all document versions and replicas in byte accounting. Compute retrieval, operation rounding and related-service charges.

findings.finding: The pricing page rounds usage up to billing units, including whole millions of operations and whole GB-months. IA has a 30-day minimum and no free tier; reads/copies incur retrieval charges.
findings.section: Billable unit rounding; Minimum storage duration
findings.effective_or_version: Page updated 2026-10-01; current retrieved prices in USD
findings.product_implication: Use the rounded model below. IA may cost more for a small document workload despite its lower storage rate; evaluate measured access patterns.

findings.finding: The compatibility table marks S3 bucket versioning, object-lock configuration, bucket policy/ACL and replication APIs unimplemented, while core object and multipart operations are supported.
findings.product_implication: Audit every RustFS/S3 feature the adapter uses. Implement logical versions as separate keys; use Cloudflare’s native permission/lock APIs rather than assuming AWS feature parity.

findings.finding: R2 bucket locks prevent overwrite/deletion by prefix for a duration, until a date or indefinitely. They cover existing/new objects and override lifecycle deletion; documented administrator operations can remove rules.
findings.section: Bucket lock rules; Notes; Remove bucket lock rules
findings.product_implication: Useful accidental-deletion protection, but do not label it S3 Object Lock compliance mode or administrator-proof legal retention. Separate runtime object rights from lock-configuration authority.

findings.topic: R2 upload identifiers and logical versions
findings.finding: R2Object.version is a random identifier associated with an upload. The Workers API gets objects by key and supports conditional writes; this field does not establish retrievable historical object versions.
findings.section: R2Object definition; Bucket methods; Conditional operations
findings.unresolved: The historical-version retrieval design is a Societyer proposal, not a native R2 feature.
findings.product_implication: Use immutable keys such as workspace/document/logicalVersion. Store hash and locator in the application database, not an assumed S3 VersionId.

findings.finding: Object reads/writes/deletes/listing are strongly consistent; competing writes have last-completion-wins behavior. API permission updates may take up to a minute. Custom-domain caches can continue serving deleted/older content.
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.product_implication: Use immutable keys and conditional/database finalization. Keep governance documents private and avoid unauthenticated caches; measure revocation propagation.

findings.finding: Data Access Logs are available for buckets without jurisdiction. They include successful/<400 object requests, exclude >=400 requests, retain seven days, and are asynchronous best effort. The page announces Observability billing from 1 December 2026.
findings.section: Overview; Turn on Data Access Logs
findings.effective_or_version: Page updated 2026-10-02; advertised Observability billing starts 2026-12-01
findings.unresolved: Availability with assigned jurisdictions is not established; advertised future billing date is not an already-effective cost.
findings.product_implication: Enable if appropriate but maintain Societyer’s complete allow/deny audit and separate retention. Do not claim vendor logs record every denied request.

findings.finding: R2 Audit Logs are free, always enabled across plans, and record listed bucket-configuration changes; object access uses the separate Data Access Logs facility.
findings.product_implication: Export relevant configuration changes and link them to connection history. Verify coverage of required actions, including retention policy changes.

findings.finding: Object Read/Write tokens can be bucket-scoped; administrative tokens can alter bucket configuration. Account tokens and user-bound tokens have different offboarding behavior.
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.product_implication: Use account-owned bucket-scoped runtime credentials or Workers bindings. Keep bucket administration out of normal application runtime roles.

findings.finding: Temporary S3 credentials are derived from a parent token, expire, and can be restricted to one bucket, operations and optional paths; they cannot exceed parent permissions.
findings.section: Choosing an approach; Scope of a credential
findings.product_implication: For multipart clients, issue narrow server-created capabilities tied to a validated upload handle. Never send parent credentials to browser/desktop clients.

findings.finding: Presigned URLs grant a single operation on one object until expiry, behave as bearer credentials, and work on the S3 API domain rather than custom domains.
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.product_implication: Authorize before minting; use short TTLs and exact keys. For immediate new-request enforcement, download through the Societyer broker.

findings.finding: R2 encrypts object content and metadata at rest using AES-256 with Cloudflare-managed keys and supports TLS in transit.
findings.section: Encryption at Rest; Encryption in Transit
findings.product_implication: Service encryption is available without client-side cryptography. Any extra key-management requirement remains a separate architecture decision.

findings.finding: Current jurisdiction choices are EU, FedRAMP and US. Geographic location hints are best-effort, and a bucket’s jurisdiction cannot be changed after creation.
findings.section: Location Hints; Available jurisdictions; Additional considerations
findings.effective_or_version: Current vendor documentation; no distinct effective date established
findings.product_implication: No reviewed R2 option establishes guaranteed Canadian residency. A North America hint is insufficient for a Canada-only commitment; choose another provider if that is a confirmed requirement.

findings.finding: R2 documents approximately 5-TiB maximum objects with exact smaller upload ceilings in footnotes, multipart up to 10,000 parts, 1,024-byte keys, 8,192-byte metadata and one write per second to the same key.
findings.product_implication: Validate the precise SDK request/part byte limits and hosting ingress limits. Version-specific keys avoid overwriting a hot object key.

findings.finding: R2 is designed for eleven-nines annual durability; its documentation explicitly distinguishes this from availability and from protection against accidental or intentional deletion.
findings.product_implication: Use independent backups with tested restores and explicit retention. Provider redundancy is not a substitute for recoverable history.

findings.finding: Super Slurper copies from S3-compatible sources, preserves custom metadata and does not delete source objects. ETags may change during migration; the documented tested-provider list does not establish RustFS testing.
findings.product_implication: Create a hash-based manifest and verify every version. Treat RustFS compatibility and historical-version completeness as tests; SharePoint needs a Graph-aware migration path.

findings.finding: R2 event notifications send create/delete events to Cloudflare Queues, consumable by Workers or HTTP pull; filters can target prefixes/suffixes.
findings.product_implication: Use events for indexing/reconciliation while keeping application audit and finalization authoritative. Include Queues/Workers costs separately.

findings.topic: Stable Microsoft identities and email semantics
findings.finding: Microsoft says email and preferred_username are mutable and unsuitable for authorization; email is not guaranteed correct. sub is pairwise to the application. oid identifies the directory object, with a different object for the same person acting in another tenant. oid plus tid supports correlation across applications within the tenant.

findings.unresolved: An upstream Entra identity differs from a Clerk or Better Auth session identity.

findings.finding: A Microsoft single-tenant application admits user and guest accounts in its home directory. Multitenant account types broaden eligible directories and optionally consumer accounts.

findings.unresolved: Whether guests are intended users, which tenant owns their object, and which guest access policies apply are private administrator decisions.

findings.unresolved: Cross-tenant trust and guest-domain SSO routing are not publicly observable.

findings.topic: Deprovisioning is not instantaneous application logout
findings.finding: Microsoft explicitly says it cannot directly revoke an application's own session token. App-local revocation/lifecycle enforcement is necessary; ordinary Entra provisioning generally runs on a 20–40-minute cycle, so upstream deletion is not an immediate app authorization guarantee.
findings.section: Session tokens; When access is revoked; Best practices
findings.unresolved: End-to-end latency depends on directory sync, broker, application caches and already issued storage URLs.
findings.product_implication: Set and measure an access-revocation objective. Reject a disabled membership on every server path and job execution, even when its session JWT remains cryptographically valid.

findings.finding: Clerk session tokens identify issuer, subject and session; version 2 also exposes pending status when relevant. Token signature success establishes authentication, not Societyer workspace authorization.

findings.finding: Microsoft distinguishes delegated permissions, requiring both user and client authorization, from app-only permissions granted to the application's own identity. Authentication alone does not grant a SharePoint library permission or Graph file access.

findings.finding: RFC 8252 requires native OAuth clients to use an external user-agent and PKCE for public native clients. Microsoft notes an offline device can retain previously downloaded data after access revocation.

findings.section: Add connection; Enforce SSO by domain; Remove member

findings.finding: Better Auth's JWT plugin documents its own JWKS endpoint and configurable issuer, audience, subject and expiry. Defaults use BASE_URL for issuer/audience and user ID for subject. These values are independent of an upstream Microsoft token.

The other listed branches have older July/August commit timestamps. This audit is of accessible main, not proof about the newer workspace described in the brief.

findings.topic: Viewer and Member grants conflict with rank ordering
findings.finding: ROLE_MATRIX contains 60 action names. Viewer receives all 28 :read actions, while Member receives 12 read actions. Viewer uniquely receives 16 additional reads including employees, conflicts, court orders, financials, users, exports, settings and audit. Separately canActAs ranks Member above Viewer. The matrix and rank hierarchy therefore are not equivalent access models.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Whether current broad Viewer grants were intentional is a product-owner decision; do not silently migrate existing workspaces.
findings.product_implication: Make action grants explicit. Proposed Viewer defaults to assigned/released read scopes; Member has member-facing read and self-service actions. Do not implement action permissions with role>=required. If broad auditor access is intended, define its exact records and fields as an explicit profile.

findings.topic: Direct member endpoints ignore write grants
findings.finding: members.create/update/remove use active same-society membership/ownership checks without checking members:write. The Convex wrappers call these handlers directly. Members and Viewers, despite having no members:write in ROLE_MATRIX, satisfy the shared membership guard when Active. Member list/get return full rows, including CRM fields such as notes, address, phone and votingRights, rather than a statutory inspection projection.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Static control flow was inspected; no request was sent to a live Convex deployment.
findings.product_implication: Add requireAction('members:write') on mutations and separately projected directory/CRM/statutory-register reads. Do not equate an app Member role to statutory membership or expose all CRM notes through legal inspection.

findings.topic: Financial read/write scope is broader than policy
findings.finding: financials.list/detailByFiscalYear require membership only; detail also returns linked documents via getOwned rather than the document ACL. financialCreate, financialUpdate and financialRemove likewise lack financials:write checks. Thus same-workspace record ownership is enforced, but action grants and document-specific confidentiality are not enforced along these paths.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Actual UI masking and deployed access were not tested.
findings.product_implication: Use the same action policy and document resolver in financial views and mutations; provide approved financial-statement extracts separately from private bookkeeping and remuneration details.

findings.topic: Governance, filing and document mutations use membership-only gates
findings.finding: Representative shared handlers for agenda create/edit/delete, meeting create/update/delete, filing create/markFiled/update/delete, bylaw-rule activation/reset, and document create/review/archive/delete rely on membership/record ownership and do not enforce the corresponding declared action grants. Their wrappers do not supply an action gate. This is a concrete discrepancy rather than a complete audit of every endpoint.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Other endpoints outside the sampled domains may have additional or different checks.
findings.product_implication: Create one requireAction helper and use it at every query/mutation/action boundary, with document-specific rules when a referenced document is returned or changed. Test direct Convex as well as REST routes.

findings.topic: Document ACL bypass in version and download paths
findings.finding: Document list/get/getMany applies canAccessDocument, but documentVersions.listForDocument/latest/get requires only parent document ownership and active membership. getDownloadUrl and getDownloadTarget call documentVersions.get then resolve/sign the content URL. Generated-workflow downloads similarly require documents:read and a version matching societyId, without the document ACL. A record hidden by the document list can remain accessible through its version identifier or generated storage key to an active member of the same workspace.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Access depends on knowing a relevant identifier and configured storage; no live content was fetched.
findings.product_implication: Require a single document action decision for metadata, version listing, downloads, previews, exports, search snippets, generated files, rollback and related-domain fetches. Apply it before minting any provider bearer URL.

findings.finding: beginUpload constructs a random server-side key and presigned upload URL. recordUploadedVersion nevertheless accepts storageProvider and storageKey from the caller, validates document ownership and Director rank, and checks only whether the key was already recorded. It does not require a server-issued upload record tying that locator to this actor/workspace/document, nor verify actual object content, size or hash before persisting supplied metadata.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Provider configuration and bucket contents were not inspected; this is a validation gap, not proof of an actual cross-workspace object disclosure.
findings.product_implication: Return an opaque upload handle; persist its actor/workspace/document/provider/key/expiry server-side; finalize only that handle after backend object verification; allowlist providers and immutable locators. Preserve atomic version allocation.

findings.topic: User role/status updates bypass active-owner invariants
findings.finding: users.upsert is Admin-gated but permits patching arbitrary role and status strings without the last-owner guard. setRole is Admin-gated and accepts a string without ROLES validation. Its owner guard counts any other row with role Owner, including Disabled. Invitation managers with Admin rank can invite any valid role, including Owner. These paths allow privilege escalation and can leave no active Owner unless additional unavailable workspace changes corrected them.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Main does not include the brief's newer role-administration implementation. No accounts were altered.
findings.product_implication: Split profile editing from role/status commands; validate enum values; only Owner can grant/revoke Admin or Owner; Admin can manage Director/Member/Viewer. Ordinary administrative demotion, removal, import, restore and bulk transitions must preserve at least one Active Owner atomically. Genuine security disabling or authoritative directory deprovisioning must always deny access, even for the last Owner; enter explicit controlled recovery instead of retaining or restoring compromised/terminated access.

findings.finding: authorizeUserRole first checks role rank, but returns success for an under-ranked active member if no peer currently has the required rank. The peer scan also ignores active status. This compatibility recovery lives in the general shared role gate and can apply to hosted authenticated principals, not only a distinct offline recovery workflow.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Whether production fixtures ever reach a stranded state is unknown.
findings.product_implication: Remove recovery from normal authorization. Use an explicit audited operator recovery workflow with verified ownership and no automatic elevation based on an empty high-role set. If security/directory disabling removes the last Active Owner, deny that identity immediately and enter this controlled recovery state; do not keep its access to satisfy an Owner-count invariant.

findings.topic: Issuer is carried but not part of identity lookup
findings.finding: The hosted adapter receives verified JWT issuer, subject and tokenIdentifier, but labels authProvider as better-auth. resolvePrincipalUser, currentPrincipalMemberships and ensureCurrentMembership query by authSubject and society only, not issuer/provider. Invitation binding stores authProvider but does not use it to resolve future memberships. This is unsafe to carry unchanged into provider migration or multiple issuers.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Only Better Auth is configured in this main snapshot, so a cross-issuer collision was not exercised.
findings.product_implication: Use a stable externalIdentity record unique on (issuer, subject), with an explicit link to an application user and separate workspace memberships. Migrate bindings with evidence; never infer authority from equal email. Use one hosted session provider per deployment.

findings.topic: Invitation acceptance has good one-use binding but missing verification/expiry
findings.finding: Invitations are workspace-bound and acceptance checks token uniqueness, revoked and accepted state, authenticated JWT issuer/subject, valid role and email equality. Neither acceptance path requires principal.emailVerified. Invitation creation stores no expiresAt value and no expiry check is present. Matching email is not itself an existing-account link, but unverified or changeable email semantics remain material to who may accept the invitation.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Provider-level account linking is separate and must be resolved with the authentication vendor; see vendor research.
findings.product_implication: Define verified acceptance evidence appropriate to Clerk/Entra claims; use expiring hashed invitation tokens, scope role grants to inviter authority, and bind acceptance to stable external identity. Retain consumed/revoked audit evidence.

findings.topic: API key scopes can outlive creator role
findings.entity: Software; REST and workflow service identity
findings.finding: REST session actions use listPermissionsForRole through roleAllows. API keys instead pass verifyToken's token/client status, expiry and stored scope checks, then gatewayApiPrincipal verifies creator existence, workspace, non-Disabled status and bound subject. The key path does not intersect the stored scope with the creator's current action grants. A still-active demoted creator can therefore retain token authority for endpoints whose shared handler checks only membership. Workflow callbacks similarly mint a user JWT from a stored run/creator binding rather than carrying explicit service action limits.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Endpoints that enforce a stricter shared role may deny some actions; no blanket claim that all demoted-key actions succeed.
findings.product_implication: As part of the P0 shared authorization gate, effective API authority must intersect active creator/service identity, current workspace action policy, key scope, record ACL and provider access on every call. Re-check queued workflow steps at execution and revoke/downgrade on status or role changes.

findings.topic: Hosted user removal requires a missing principal field
findings.finding: users.remove derives societyId only from portableCtx.principal.societyId and throws if absent. hostedPrincipal in convex/lib/portable.ts does not set societyId. Static control flow therefore indicates normal hosted JWT removal fails before target membership/Owner checks, even for an authorized Owner.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: A live hosted removal request was deliberately not attempted.
findings.product_implication: Resolve the target row, derive its workspace, and authorize the verified principal against that workspace in one transaction. Do not rely on a client-supplied active workspace or optional principal field.

findings.topic: Permission introspection is not a trusted self-check
findings.finding: myPermissionsPortable returns role/action grants for any supplied userId in the supplied society without verifying the current principal or current membership status. convex.permissions.check similarly accepts a target user ID. The legacy requirePermission helper trusts userId rather than deriving a verified actor. users.list/get authorize any active workspace member and return raw user rows even though Member lacks users:read.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: These helpers return policy information, not raw auth credentials; impact is role/identity disclosure and unsafe future reuse.
findings.product_implication: Derive the subject from the verified runtime principal for self permissions; protect administrative inspection separately. Expose safe projections and never use the existing caller-ID helper as a substitute for principal-bound requireAction.

findings.topic: Status checks are inconsistent across boundaries
findings.finding: requireSocietyMembership rejects every nonempty status except Active, while accepting missing status for legacy compatibility. Invitation manager and gateway identity lookups reject Disabled specifically but can accept other status strings. ensureCurrentMembership returns bound for existing statuses other than Disabled. Core record handlers generally re-check stricter membership, but status policy is not uniform across all entry points.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Do not claim Disabled users have general live access; the ordinary membership guard explicitly blocks them.
findings.product_implication: Normalize statuses with explicit Active eligibility, migrate legacy missing values, and deny Invited/Suspended/Disabled/Removed principals consistently. Revoke active key and workflow execution authority; keep inspection-entitlement fulfillment separate from login restoration. Security/directory disabling also applies to the last Owner and must enter controlled recovery if no Active Owner remains, never preserve the disabled account access.

findings.topic: Main auth implementation differs from the brief
findings.finding: server/auth-config.ts supports none or better-auth, enables email/password and a JWT plugin; no Microsoft social provider is configured there. Convex registers the Better Auth ES256 issuer/JWKS. package.json declares better-auth ^1.6.3 and package-lock resolves 1.6.23. Clerk and Microsoft SSO files named by the brief are absent.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: The live deployed package/runtime version is not known.
findings.product_implication: Treat Clerk/Microsoft comparison as a forward migration plan until the newer working files are supplied. Preserve Societyer membership/roles, replace the session verifier at every frontend/Convex/REST boundary, and check current advisories and upgrade migrations.

findings.topic: Local mode is a separate trust model
findings.finding: AuthProvider intentionally uses NoAuthProvider for local data runtimes. Local workspace adapters mint trusted-workspace identities bound to the local workspace; the access layer may choose an Owner or synthetic Owner for societies in the same local file. The local data holder is therefore the authority. This is distinct from hosted per-user access and is not a secure multi-user tenant boundary by itself.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: OS/filesystem protection and desktop secret handling were not penetration-tested.
findings.product_implication: Document local single-operator trust explicitly, protect files and exports, and require a fresh hosted authentication/membership binding when importing or promoting local data. Never accept serialized trusted-workspace assurance from a hosted client.

findings.topic: Current storage supports RustFS/demo and local/native paths
findings.finding: Configured hosted storage selects rustfs or demo based on deployment environment. The shared signer creates SigV4 GET URLs with 900-second expiry; upload adapter also uses 900 seconds. The frontend document-storage interface primarily covers local filesystem targets. SharePoint, Graph and R2 are not implemented provider adapters in these reviewed code paths.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Private tenant, bucket, licence, retention and storage deployment settings were not inspected.
findings.product_implication: Introduce a per-workspace storage binding and per-document authoritative provider record, with server-only credentials and provider-specific IDs/version references. Reuse the S3 path only after R2 compatibility tests; do not equate an endpoint change with a completed provider integration.

findings.topic: Generic bylaw defaults remain shared across entity types
findings.finding: DEFAULT_BYLAW_RULES includes 14–60 notice days, 10% quorum with minimum 3, proxies disabled, annualReportDueDaysAfterMeeting 30, ordinary 50 and special 66.67. Equivalent defaults are duplicated in shared/functions/meetings.ts and convex/lib/bylawRules.ts. The accessible reset handler has no entity/statute guard and the UI labels it a BC Model Bylaw baseline. These are application defaults, not verified universal legal rules.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: No assertion is made that every listed number is wrong for every BC society. Exact statutory/default/custom distinctions are in the legal research.
findings.product_implication: Centralize dated entity/statute/subtype rule resolution. Unknown corporation settings should be unresolved until verified or adopted; prevent a society baseline reset from changing corporation rules. Retain operative bylaws/articles plus adoption evidence. Reconcile the newer guard described in the brief.

findings.finding: BC_REGISTRY_URL is set to the societies path and is reused for BCCompanyAnnualReport and BCExtraProvincialAnnualReport. The brief says these links and displays have been separated; that newer separation is not present in accessible main.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Whether redirects happen to land on a working company flow was not tested; legal agents independently verified filing channels.
findings.product_implication: Select registry channel by entity, subtype, registration context and current government guidance; do not use one BC portal constant for all entities.

findings.topic: CBCA initial ISC schedule conflates incorporation with continuance/amalgamation
findings.finding: The current CBCA rule initial-isc-filing uses incorporationDate with a 30-day offset and describes incorporation, amalgamation and continuance together. Federal research verifies that the incorporation filing is part of incorporation, while the 30-day period applies after certificate of amalgamation or continuance.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: The legal supporting primary source belongs in the federal report; code itself is not legal authority.
findings.product_implication: Split initial events and schedule incorporation ISC as a required formation input/completion condition; retain separate certificate-triggered 30-day events where applicable.

findings.topic: Ontario initial return uses a overloaded date anchor
findings.finding: The Ontario initial-return rule applies to home and extra_provincial contexts and uses incorporationDate+60. complianceFactsForRegistration sets incorporationDate to registrationDate first, then activityCommencementDate, then home incorporation date. It separately stores commencedBusinessDate but the rule does not use it. The legal trigger for extra-provincial initial return is beginning business in Ontario.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Federal/Ontario legal research supplies the verified primary legal/form instructions.
findings.product_implication: Use distinct home-incorporation and Ontario-business-commencement event fields/rules. Missing commencement date should request evidence rather than substitute the registration/home-incorporation date.

findings.topic: Recurring computation only returns a next cycle
findings.finding: computeAnnualDueDate and recurring computeWindowDates increment years while dueDate is before asOfDate. Consequently those helpers return the next future/current annual occurrence rather than a prior overdue occurrence. A complete compliance view therefore needs a separate persisted cycle/completion history; these functions alone cannot preserve unfiled prior annual periods.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Whether another UI/ledger compensates for this helper behavior was not exhaustively audited; this is a confirmed helper behavior and an end-to-end risk to verify.
findings.product_implication: Persist obligations by organization+registration+rule+cycle and reconcile completion evidence. Keep overdue unresolved cycles visible beside next-cycle planning.

findings.topic: Rule source-review gates already exist; applicability still needs legal semantics
findings.finding: The schema already requires applicability/source IDs for non-deprecated rules, reviewer/date for reviewed or accepted rules, and approver/date/reference for accepted rules. Source records carry retrieval/effective dates. This is an implemented strength, unlike the older research note's initial gap list. However rule-level legalForce, trigger exceptions, operative provision effective range and a missing-fact decision model are not fields in the reviewed rule schema.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Pack reviewedAt is not proof of legal approval; all reviewed jurisdiction packs remain marked draft.
findings.product_implication: Keep existing review gates; add required/conditional/recommended/operational distinction, dated applicability exceptions, effective provision version, evidence-to-trigger links and no-silent-fallback date rules. Do not mark all rules accepted just because this research supplies links.

findings.topic: Cross-entity packet guard is absent on accessible main
findings.finding: generatePacketForSocietyPortable selects a corporation or society packet solely from requested packetKey and seeds that catalog. generateDocumentFromCatalogPortable checks membership then calls it. Seed-by-entity routing exists but does not validate the entity when later generating a chosen packet. The brief's cross-mode blocking is therefore not verifiable in main.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Generated drafts were not reviewed for jurisdiction-specific legal suitability.
findings.product_implication: Require entity/statute/subtype compatibility at every generation/staging boundary, not only catalog UI filtering; persist source template/version and draft/adopted status. Reconcile newer working changes before implementing.

findings.topic: Module settings are feature configuration, not permission grants
findings.finding: src/lib/modules.ts normalizes disabled module keys into booleans; recordPermissions.ts uses requiredModules/readableRoles/updatableRoles as client-side configuration. The reviewed membership-only server handlers do not call the module/action matrix. The newer moduleAccess.ts named in the brief is missing.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Individual module override behavior described in the newer workspace was not available to inspect.
findings.product_implication: Keep module visibility distinct from security. If a disabled feature must reject API use, express that as a separate server-side feature-availability predicate; it must never grant access. Implement explicit per-action policy before optional per-person module overrides.

findings.topic: Vote denominator approximation is unsafe for legal conclusions
findings.finding: motionGovernance correctly treats simple majority as strictly greater than half and snaps rounded 66.67 to exact two thirds. However motionCarriesByType explicitly approximates eligibleMembers or quorum bases as votesCast when its inline context lacks the proper denominator. That can display a pass/fail result using a different electorate than the configured rule.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Actual persisted adoption workflows and corporate share-class vote handling require further review.
findings.product_implication: Represent the denominator and threshold exactly; require eligible membership/share voting rights, class votes, record date, quorum and exclusions where applicable. Return not-evaluable when required context is missing. Do not report the existing 66.67 display as a confirmed arithmetic defect.

findings.topic: Committee access uses mutable label matching
findings.finding: Document access context treats a committee row as belonging to a user when memberId/directorId matches OR normalized email matches OR normalized name equals the user's displayName. Name equality is not an authenticated committee assignment; users with duplicate or changed display names can receive unintended committee-derived access.
findings.confidence: High: verified static source; not a live deployment test
findings.unresolved: Whether any existing workspace has ambiguous name/email assignments is unknown.
findings.product_implication: Migrate label matches into a reviewed identity-resolution queue; store explicit user/member/director-to-committee bindings with validity dates. Runtime authorization must use stable bound IDs only.

backlog.item: Resolve Clerk's provider-level same-email linking before migration or strict enterprise rollout.
backlog.reason: Clerk's documented social and enterprise linking can merge identities before Societyer sees a subject. Local issuer+subject binding alone cannot prevent that behavior.

backlog.acceptance: Same email under two distinct upstream accounts cannot acquire another account's Societyer memberships without explicit authorized proof; all enabled OAuth, SSO and directory-provisioning paths are tested, or the exception is explicitly accepted and documented.
backlog.verification: Controlled duplicate-email tests across tenants, social/SSO switching, account recreation, and SCIM provisioning; vendor documentation/response retained.

backlog.item: Reconcile the published acceptMappedClaims configuration conflict.
backlog.reason: Clerk's multitenant Microsoft recipe sets the field true; Microsoft warns against true for multitenant applications.
backlog.dependency: Company administrator and supported Clerk/Entra configuration; selected social versus tenant-bound enterprise design.
backlog.acceptance: Published Societyer setup instructions contain no unsupported claims-mapping workaround; actual issued claims, issuer, audience and signatures validate under a documented minimal configuration.
backlog.verification: Review the app manifest and signed test tokens in an approved tenant; demonstrate wrong-tenant/mapped-claim rejection without exposing token contents or credentials.

backlog.item: Require exactly one hosted session broker and issuer-aware principal lookup.
backlog.reason: Multiple environment flags or subject-only membership lookup can disagree across frontend, Convex and gateway.
backlog.dependency: Newer workspace/branch containing the brief's Clerk and Microsoft implementations; exact deployed config.
backlog.acceptance: Hosted startup rejects missing/contradictory providers; all user requests map an allowlisted issuer plus exact subject to one immutable local user ID. Auth-disabled/local mode cannot reach hosted resources.
backlog.verification: A token with matching sub from another issuer, wrong audience, invalid signature, expired time, disallowed origin or pending session fails on every public endpoint.

backlog.item: Apply active membership, role/action and record rules on sessions, API keys and workflows.
backlog.reason: Valid sign-in or a long-lived key does not establish current Societyer authorization; a disabled account must lose access even before JWT expiry.
backlog.dependency: One centralized authorization policy and membership status model.
backlog.acceptance: All protected reads/writes, exports, downloads and queued jobs require the same current access predicate. API-key scopes are intersected with current owning user permissions unless the key belongs to an explicit service principal.
backlog.verification: Role downgrade, workspace removal and status transition immediately deny previously authorized user keys and queued work at execution time; cross-workspace IDs fail.

backlog.item: Specify and test enterprise SSO policy without inferring organization from email.
backlog.reason: Clerk Microsoft social is common-only; Entra single tenant includes guests; upstream assignment has exceptions and cannot replace app membership.
backlog.dependency: Verified tenant UUID, approved guests, chosen SAML/OIDC connection, supported session-level SSO evidence.
backlog.acceptance: Approved member and approved guest can complete intended flows; personal/foreign-tenant/unassigned or locally uninvited identities gain no workspace rights. Existing non-SSO sessions cannot bypass an SSO-required workspace.
backlog.verification: Positive/negative member, guest, same-email-other-tenant, removed guest, old-session and app-administrator scenarios.

backlog.item: Add BC subtype and actual registry/migration state; update links using September 2026 guidance.

backlog.acceptance: Named/numbered ordinary and benefit paths route correctly; unreviewed special subtype automation is held for review; official links are dated.
backlog.verification: Check public official guide and live entry points; no real filing needed.

backlog.verification: Review synthetic one-founder, two-founder, multi-class and numbered cases with legal reviewer; compare to official Form 1 fields.

backlog.verification: Test a shareholder without account, app Member without shares, proxy holder, corporate shareholder representative and interested director.

backlog.acceptance: All s13 inputs; valid name; qualified/consenting director roster; model/custom bylaws; authorized filer; $130 base plus separate fees; certificate activates registration.

backlog.verification: Forged key/connection, replay, mismatched size/hash, expired handle and orphan-reconciliation tests.
